* Cloudflare (NYSE:NET ) fell over 18% ahead of the opening bell as investors see the company belatedly playing catch-up on AI, with management noting it’s “the biggest tailwind we’ve ever seen,” along with quarterly results showing a 4.67% fall in gross profit margins from the prior-year period.

items.title: Item 1
items.text: Cloudflare Sinks on AI Reform ******************************** Cloudflare (NYSE:NET ) fell over 18% ahead of the opening bell as investors see the company belatedly playing catch-up on AI, with management noting it’s “the biggest tailwind we’ve ever seen,” along with quarterly results showing a 4.67% fall in gross profit margins from the prior-year period. * “Cloudflare’s usage of AI has increased by more than 600% in the last three months alone”: 1,100 staff are being cut, with an email sent to staff saying management “have to be intentional in how we architect our company for the agentic AI era,” with the job cuts representing 20% of the current workforce. * News overshadows strong set of results: Despite the fall in gross margin, revenue rose by 34% versus the same period last year, with the outlook for full-year fiscal 2026 revenue and earnings raised. The stock is outperforming the S&P 500 by 285% since the November 2022 Stock Advisor recommendation by Team Hidden Gems. items.title: Item 2
items.text:
SA Results From HUBS, MNST, RKLB, and NTDOY ---------------------------------------------- * HubSpot (NYSE:HUBS ) slumped around 20% in pre-market trading as results provided some concern over future revenue growth rates and broader valuation concerns, despite profitability for the quarter improving year over year (YoY) for the recommendation by Team HG. * Monster Beverage (NASDAQ:MNST ) popped over 6% in pre-market trading thanks to the Team RB rec reporting record quarterly sales , helped out by international growth and energy drink demand. * Nintendo (OTC:NTDOY ) disappointed investors as results forecasted a decline in sales for its flagship console, the Switch 2, as memory chip shortages bite at the Team Rule Breakers recommendation. * Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB ) jumped over 6% ahead of the opening bell as results beat its own financial forecasts , with the Team Hidden Gems rec signing multiple new launch contracts. Fool contributing analyst Lou Whiteman said “there is nothing in the report to suggest Rocket Lab isn't on its way toward growing into the company the market expects in the years to come.” Examine Lou’s full RKLB breakdown A message from The Motley Fool

Let's be honest, if you’re an investor who didn't buy Nvidia five years ago, you probably missed out on the 4,704% run.

But here's the good news: Nvidia was just a Phase One company. Now it built the infrastructure. The picks and shovels. The runway for Artificial Intelligence to run free.

Phase Two – where companies actually use all that infrastructure to build products, platforms, and services – is just beginning. 

And historically, that's where the biggest winners of any tech boom emerge. Netflix didn't lay the fiber optic cables. It used them. And returned over 43,000% since 2004.

Our analysts have identified five Phase Two AI companies — most of them a fraction of Nvidia's size — positioned for what comes next. You can see all five names and why we picked them in a new report, available with an Epic membership.

items.title: Item 3
items.text: Record AI Capex Cycle Drains Tech Cash ***************************************** New data from Visible Alpha shows the tech sector is facing the biggest cash strain in over a decade, as record-breaking AI capex spend weighs on free cash flow, even with higher spending in the pipeline. * Full-year free cash flow set to hit lowest level since 2014: The combined free cash flow of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN ), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG ), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT ), and Meta (NASDAQ:META ) is due to fall to around $4 billion in Q3, a stark drop from the $45 billion average for each quarter since the pandemic. * AI buildout seen as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity: Amazon is expected to spend more cash than it generates this year, with other tech stocks in a similar position. Investors will need to weigh up whether such spending can result in higher returns down the road. Review this month’s Mag 7 earnings --------------------------
